text: I am sorry the imaging and specific blood sugar results are unavailable; to determine if this is a venous stasis ulcer, arterial insufficiency, or a diabetic foot ulcer, can you describe the wound's color, depth, and if the surrounding skin feels warm or is hard to the touch? Please confirm if you have a known history of deep vein thrombosis, varicose veins, or peripheral artery disease.

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your 10-year history of chronic leg swelling and prior DVT, the strong family history suggests a genetic predisposition to venous issues. Does the wound appear to have a raised, rolled edge, and does the surrounding skin have a dark, brownish discoloration or feel hard and thickened? Please also describe if the pain or swelling worsens significantly when you stand for long periods and improves when you lie down with your legs elevated.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your 10-year history of chronic swelling, prior DVT, and family history, the clinical picture strongly points to venous insufficiency. To confirm the specific type of ulcer, does the wound have a "rolled" or raised edge, and is the surrounding skin dark brown or hardened (lipodermatosclerosis)? Does the pain or swelling get significantly worse when you stand for long periods and improve when you lie down with your legs elevated?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
